title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 208
paragraphs: While they were deliberating, Xerxes sent a mounted scout to see how many they were and what they were doing. For he had heard while still in Thessaly that a small force had gathered at this spot, led by Lacedaemonians, with Leonidas — who was of the line of Heracles — at their head. When the horseman rode up toward their camp, he could see them, but not the whole army: those posted within the wall that they had repaired and were guarding could not be seen, but he observed those outside, whose station was in front of the wall. It happened at that moment that the Lacedaemonians were the ones posted outside. So he saw some of the men practicing athletic exercises and others combing their long hair; and as he looked upon these things he marveled, while also taking careful note of their number. When he had observed everything exactly, he rode back unmolested, for no one tried to pursue him, and he found himself treated with complete indifference. On his return, he reported to Xerxes everything he had seen.
